access_links.label: Code and Brisbane proof-of-concept on GitHub

description: ATAM, the Active Transport Analytics Model, is a strategic transport modelling and visualisation framework for walking, cycling and emerging micromobility. A proof of concept was built for cycling in Brisbane, Queensland. Networks are a key input and can be curated from OpenStreetMap and other open data with attributes such as safety for active travel users, so future network changes can be tested for project appraisal. Demand matrices are the other input: base year demand can come from household travel surveys, counts, Strava or mobility data, or other strategic models, and future demand from demographic projections. Outputs are link volumes, journey times by route and origin-destination matrix, and select link analysis. The model uses open-source tools, Python and QGIS, with Tableau Public for visualisation, and needs no proprietary transport modelling software. Coverage: Brisbane in the proof of concept; other regions need their own networks and demand. Format and access: code and example data on GitHub, and a project website. Licence and cost: MIT, free. Caveats: a proof of concept by a small team, with no calibration or validation reported. It supports network flow and capacity planning for cycling infrastructure. It can use Strava Metro data and complements the PeopleForBikes network analysis in the catalogue.
